clusters.text: At least 68 people have been killed and dozens injured after a high-speed train collision in Spain’s central province of Toledo. Videos and photographs from the scene showed overturned carriages, injured passengers and emergency crews working to rescue people trapped in the wreckage.The collision occurred on Wednesday morning near Urda, about 120 km south of Madrid, on the Madrid-Seville rail route. Recordings captured by passengers showed scenes inside the trains following the impact, while images from the site showed carriages lying on their sides beside the tracks.Emergency services rushed to the scene to evacuate passengers, provide medical assistance and search the wreckage for survivors. Injured passengers were taken to nearby medical facilities, including a sports centre converted into a temporary treatment site. The regional government of Castilla-La Mancha said 58 people were receiving treatment in hospitals.According to Spain’s rail infrastructure operator ADIF, both trains were travelling south from Madrid towards Seville when the collision occurred. A state-owned RENFE train struck the rear of an IRYO train that had stopped on the tracks, derailing carriages on both trains.Spain’s transport minister Óscar Puente said a failure in the railway’s computer communications system had disrupted safety operations before the collision. The malfunction automatically stopped trains along a 63-kilometre stretch of track, after which the RENFE train was reportedly allowed to proceed despite a red signal.According to accounts of the incident, ADIF took manual control of the system following the failure. Puente said the train was authorised to continue under circumstances that investigators would need to examine.“There was a red signal prohibiting movement, yet the train was authorized to proceed,” Puente said at a press conference on Wednesday. “It is a decision made under inexplicable circumstances.”The RENFE train reportedly resumed its journey at about 124 miles per hour before hitting the stationary IRYO train. Authorities have yet to establish the full sequence of events leading to the crash.Meanwhile, Spanish trade union CSIF has demanded the resignation of the transport minister following the collision. clusters.snippet: The Vera Rubin Observatory has discovered a suspected dwarf planet beyond Neptune's orbit. If confirmed, it would be the sixth known dwarf planet in our solar system.

Astronomers found a mysterious object beyond Neptune, and it could be a new dwarf planet
clusters.text: For years, Pluto held a place among the solar system’s nine planets, until its status changed in 2006. Now, a newly discovered icy object lurking beyond Pluto has reignited interest in the distant worlds at the edge of our solar system and the question of what qualifies as a planet.Named 2026 ED138, the object was detected using the Vera C Rubin Observatory in Chile, but further observations are needed to confirm whether it qualifies as a dwarf planet. The discovery was announced at a scientific meeting in Spokane, Washington.Researchers estimate that 2026 ED138 is between 600 and 1,500 km wide and orbits the Sun at a distance roughly 46 times that between Earth and the Sun. Pluto, by comparison, orbits at an average distance of about 40 times the Earth-Sun distance.If confirmed as a dwarf planet, 2026 ED138 would join five objects currently recognised in that category by the International Astronomical Union (IAU): Pluto, Eris, Haumea, Makemake and Ceres. While Pluto, Eris, Haumea and Makemake orbit beyond Neptune, Ceres is located in the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter.What qualifies as a dwarf planet?Astrophysicist Matt Holman of the Center for Astrophysics, Harvard & Smithsonian, who first spotted 2026 ED138, told Reuters that the discovery highlights the potential for further findings with the Rubin Observatory and other telescopes.As per the information available, scientists still need to establish the object's actual size. Current observations capture sunlight reflected from its surface, making it difficult to distinguish between a smaller, highly reflective object and a larger, less reflective one. Observations using Chile's Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA), which can detect light emitted by the object itself, could help researchers measure its size more accurately.To qualify as a dwarf planet, an object must have enough mass for its own gravity to pull it into a nearly round shape. Although 2026 ED138 appears to meet this requirement, further observations are needed to confirm its classification.Pluto was reclassified from the solar system's ninth planet to a dwarf planet by the IAU in 2006 because it did not meet the organisation's formal definition of a planet. He was speaking at a webinar on ‘The Golden Hour: Every Minute Matters, Every Life Counts’, presented by Kauvery Hospital in association with The Hindu to mark World Stroke Day, observed annually on October 29. He was joined by Harish R. Kamath, consultant neurologist, Kauvery Hosur. The experts stressed on the need for timely access to care as time is the most crucial factor to salvage the brain. Treatment of stroke has transformed tremendously, and families need to be aware, Dr. Thandeswaran added. In his presentation, Dr. Kamath explained the symptoms of stroke, including loss of balance, blurring vision, facial asymmetry, weakness in arms, and slurring speech. He said 1.8 million new stroke cases are added every year and 7.25 million deaths due to stroke occur every year. Dr. Thandeswaran said that while big city hospitals have facilities for scanning, imaging, and treatment, including thrombolysis (dissolving blood clots with medicine) and thrombectomy (removing clot through surgery), in remote areas, telemedicine and video calls were being used in identifying stroke patients and transferring them to Comprehensive Stroke Centres, where advanced services and specialist teams are available. Maybe he thought it’d sound more impressive to investors and the general public. Shahram Mokhtari, the lead teardown technician at iFixit explained to The Verge that part of the “extremely sensitive” flexible inner screen is pushing up against the hinge. clusters.text: Tarik Muharemovic had one season in Europe's top leagues before signing for Leeds in July "He did a tackle right in front of the South Stand and the whole place erupted. I was thinking, 'you're going to go down well with this club'." Former Leeds United boss Simon Grayson is reflecting on the moment new signing Tarik Muharemovic endeared himself to fans on his Elland Road debut in a friendly against RB Leipzig in July. The 23-year-old defender had just become Leeds ' most expensive defender following a £34.1m move from Italian side Sassuolo, replacing the long-serving Pascal Struijk, who joined Brighton for £20m. At the time, some supporters questioned the fee for a player with only one season under his belt in Europe's top leagues. "He's the right profile but the price is a bit steep," wrote one after the signing of the 6ft 4in left-footed centre-back. Another added: "Seems like another sensible addition although the fee is eye-watering." Three months into a five-year contract and talk has quickly turned to how long Leeds can keep Muharemovic, such has been his impact since arriving from an impressive World Cup with Bosnia-Herzegovina. "Muharemovic has done that well that there will already be clubs looking at him, trying to nick him over the next few months," former Leeds United striker Lucy Ward told BBC Sport. Jonny Buchan, presenter of the BBC's Don't Go To Bed Just Yet Leeds United podcast, added: "There could be a fear he is a one-year wonder with Leeds in that he does that well in the Premier League, raises his profile that much, that clubs will come for him." There is already reported interest from Barcelona, , external Liverpool , Bayern Munich and Inter Milan in Muharemovic, who has earned praise for his no-nonsense approach to defending as well as his aerial presence at both ends of the pitch. Grayson, who managed Leeds from 2008 to 2012, said he has proved a "rock-like" presence and a prolonged spell at Elland Road will benefit the player in the long run. "I'm not daft enough to think he doesn't have aspirations to one day play for some of the biggest clubs in the world," Grayson told BBC Sport. "But right now? Sometimes a player is at home with a certain club and I get that feeling with Muharemovic. I get the impression he loves Leeds , he loves the city and he loves the supporters." clusters.text: BENGALURU: Vishnuprasad paid Rs 12,500 every month for 40 months to complete a Rs 5 lakh chit fund scheme run by Samith Chits Pvt Ltd. But after he won the bid in May 2025, the company paid him only Rs 20,000, leaving Rs 4,07,940 unpaid.The consumer commission has now directed the company to pay the outstanding amount with 6.5% annual interest from the date the consumer complaint was filed until realisation. It has also ordered Samith Chits to pay Rs 3,000 towards proceedings costs, holding that the failure to pay the prize money amounted to deficiency in service and an unfair trade practice.President Syed Anser Khaleem and two members pronounced the order on September 28, 2026.According to the complaint, Vishnuprasad's chit scheme ended in June 2025. After he successfully bid for the chit in May, the company issued two cheques towards the amount due — one for Rs 1 lakh, dated July 5, 2025, and another for Rs 3,27,940, dated July 15, 2025.Vishnuprasad presented the first cheque on July 17 through his bank account in Ramamurthy Nagar. It was returned unpaid with the endorsement "Funds Insufficient". The second cheque, presented on July 24, was also dishonoured for insufficient funds.After receiving only Rs 20,000 despite follow-ups, Vishnuprasad issued a legal notice under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, which deals with cheque dishonour. He also initiated two cases before the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate court in Bengaluru, numbered CC No. 72718/2025 and CC No. 72660/2025, before approaching the consumer commission.The commission examined Vishnuprasad's affidavit and supporting documents, including the company's brochure, its statement, copies of the cheques and records confirming their dishonour.Samith Chits did not appear despite being served notice and was placed ex parte on July 24, 2026. With the complaint and supporting evidence undisputed in the consumer proceedings, the commission held the company liable for failing to pay the outstanding chit amount.It also clarified that the cheque-dishonour cases did not prevent Vishnuprasad from seeking relief under consumer protection law. also: Allahabad HC orders demolition of illegal towers at Ghaziabad's Gulmohar Greens
Allahabad HC Orders Demolition Of 2 Towers At Ghaziabad's Gulmohar Greens Society, Builder Fined ₹25 Lakh
clusters.text: Prayagraj, Oct 28 (PTI) The Allahabad High Court has directed the demolition of entire tower numbers 27 and 28 and ninth and tenth floors of tower numbers 16, 17, 18 and 19 of Gulmohar Greens Residential Society in Ghaziabad. A bench comprising Justice Saral Srivastava and Justice Sudhanshu Chauhan on Tuesday directed the Ghaziabad Development Authority (GDA) to carry out the demolitions within two months. “We also permit GDA to recover the expenses incurred in demolition from the promoter as arrears of land revenue. We further direct the district administration as well as police authorities to provide adequate assistance and security to the officers of GDA at the time of carrying out demolition in compliance with this order,” the court added. The direction was passed while hearing a petition filed by the owners and residents of the apartment situated at Gulmohar Greens Residential Society, Katori Mill, Mohan Nagar in Sahibabad, who had moved court challenging the compounding map against them. In its 95-page judgment, the court observed that the project had started in the year 2005 but it has not been completed even though more than 20 years have passed. The promoter has not obtained the completion certificate despite the fact that under the Uttar Pradesh Apartment Act, 2010, the responsibility to obtain completion certificate is of the promoter. “In such a pitiable situation, we cannot expect the apartment owners — who have invested their hard-earned money and on many occasions have managed the funds from finance companies, financial institutions or banks with a liability — to pay EMIs on getting the loan sanctioned, which begins immediately after loan amount is paid to the promoter,” the court added. “In such a situation, the apartment owner cannot afford to wait till the time the promoter obtains the completion certificate. Because of these compulsions and constraints, the apartment owners have no option but to occupy the apartments to ease out their financial burden.” The court also observed that Inspector Surendera Singh has not conducted the investigation properly and fairly, and thus has failed to discharge his duty properly. “In such view of the fact, we suspend Inspector Surendera Singh and direct the competent authority to hold an inquiry against him for dereliction of duty,” it said. clusters.title: SIT to probe lawyer-doctor clash at SRN Hospital in Prayagraj | Hindustan Times
also: SIT formed to probe lawyer-doctor clash at Prayagraj hospital | Tap to know more | Inshorts
clusters.text: A special investigation team (SIT) will probe the alleged assault on advocate Sarvesh Shukla at the trauma centre of SRN Hospital and the subsequent clashes involving assistant professor Dr Vibhu Mishra and medical students during a protest by lawyers. The police administration constituted the SIT late Tuesday night to ensure an impartial investigation into allegations made by both sides.The three-member team, comprising an inspector and two sub-inspectors, will function under the supervision of an assistant commissioner of police (ACP). It will examine the allegations, collect evidence and establish the sequence of events before further legal action is taken on the basis of its findings, officials said.Additional commissioner of police Vijay Dhull said cases had been registered on complaints from both sides, with serious allegations levelled by each. The SIT has been formed to ensure a fair investigation into all aspects of the incident, he added.The controversy dates back to the night of October 22, when a dispute over treatment at the hospital’s trauma centre allegedly led to the assault on advocate Sarvesh Shukla and his driver. Lawyers later staged a protest on October 26, blocking traffic from the hospital gate to Mahatma Gandhi Marg, alleging that no legal action had been taken despite the registration of a case.The protest disrupted traffic in the city and affected the outpatient department (OPD) and emergency services at SRN Hospital.Meanwhile, Dr Vibhu Mishra, an assistant professor at the medical college, accused lawyers of assault and looting during the protest. An FIR was registered at George Town police station on October 26 night on the basis of his complaint. Allegations were also levelled regarding the assault on eight medical students.The police administration held talks with a delegation of lawyers on Tuesday. With the formation of the SIT, the allegations in both cases, available evidence and the sequence of events will now be examined as part of the investigation.

clusters.title: Ranchi Assistant Jailer Tests Deferred Over Heavy Rain Threat
also: Heavy rain threat makes JSSC defer physical tests for assistant jailer posts
clusters.text: The Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC) has postponed the physical measurement and physical efficiency tests for assistant jailer recruitment in Ranchi after police authorities warned of heavy rainfall linked to Cyclone Arnab. The tests scheduled from October 28 to 31 at the JAP-1 Ground in Doranda will now be held on November 18, 19, 20 and 21 respectively. The decision affects candidates assigned to Selection Board-01 under the Jharkhand Assistant Jailer Competitive Examination-2025, which has 45 vacancies. JSSC said the day-wise sequence would remain unchanged, meaning candidates scheduled for each original date will appear on the corresponding rescheduled date in November. According to the commission’s notification issued on Wednesday, the postponement followed communications from the offices of the director general and inspector general of police regarding the likelihood of heavy rainfall in Ranchi under the influence of the cyclone. The physical tests require candidates to report to an outdoor ground, making weather and ground conditions important operational factors for the examination authorities. More than 50,000 candidates are expected to appear for the physical tests, according to sources cited in the report. The scale of participation means that the change affects not only candidates but also the arrangements for reporting, verification and crowd management at the examination venue. JSSC clarified that the revised schedule applies only to candidates assigned to Selection Board-01. Physical measurement and physical efficiency tests being conducted through the other three selection boards across Jharkhand will continue as scheduled, according to the commission’s notification. Candidates appearing for the rescheduled tests will not be required to download fresh admit cards. JSSC said all other provisions contained in its notifications issued on October 16 and October 22 would remain unchanged. The commission has advised candidates to regularly monitor its official website for further updates related to the recruitment process. The postponement illustrates the administrative impact of severe-weather warnings on large outdoor public exercises. clusters.snippet: Air India has chosen its long-trusted partner, SBI Cards, to issue its co-branded credit card in the coming months. Here are the details of this new partnership. The post Air India Maharaja Club and SBI Card announce a new co-branded credit card partnership appeared first on Live
also: Air India Maharaja Club and SBI Card announce a new co-branded credit card partnership
clusters.text: Air India’s Maharaja Club and SBI Card are teaming up again to launch a new co-branded credit card. Announced on October 28, 2026, the new partnership will bring together Air India’s Maharaja Club frequent flyer programme, SBI Card’s credit card business, and Visa’s global payment network to create a travel-focused credit card for Indian consumers, just like the one in existence since 2013 and the one that came to be with Vistara . Air India says the new card will reward customers for everyday spending as well as their travel and lifestyle aspirations. That is a fairly broad promise, but the opportunity is interesting. Maharaja Club has been rebuilt over the past couple of years, and a well-designed credit card could give the loyalty programme a stronger presence in Indian consumers’ wallets, which many folks are looking forward to. This is not the first time Air India and SBI Card have worked together on a co-branded credit card. The two companies introduced the Air India SBI Platinum Card and the Air India SBI Signature Card in 2013, giving Indian consumers a way to earn rewards through credit card spending and turn those rewards into value for air travel. The earlier cards were built around Air India’s frequent flyer programme, then known as Flying Returns. The proposition was fairly straightforward: earn reward points on everyday purchases, earn accelerated rewards when buying eligible Air India tickets, and eventually use the accumulated points towards air travel. The Platinum and Signature variants offered different earning rates and benefits. At launch, the Platinum card earned two reward points for every INR 100 spent and ten points per INR 100 spent on Air India bookings through the airline’s website and booking offices. It also offered annual-spend bonuses and premium benefits such as complimentary lounge access and status. The Signature card sat higher in the product hierarchy, with a more generous reward structure and additional privileges for customers who spent more. Over time, the cards changed their benefits and reward structures. SBI Card eventually stopped issuing new Air India SBI Platinum and Signature cards, effective October 10, 2024. Today’s announcement therefore represents a return to the drawing board for both companies, rather than an entirely new relationship. However, a complete new RFP was done to arrive at this decision. clusters.title: Salesforce in talks to lease Tel Aviv office space in ToHa2
clusters.text: US enterprise software giant Salesforce is in advanced talks to rent office space in the ToHa2 tower in Tel Aviv. Sources have told "Globes" that the company is seeking to lease floors 4-5, totaling 15,000 square meters in the tower. The company has about 1,000 employees in Israel, who are currently spread across three Tel Aviv office towers - Alon Tower 1, Azrieli Sarona Tower, and ToHa 1 as well as in Nazareth but in the future will be consolidated into a single location. The tower is being constructed by Amot Investments and Bayside (Gav-Yam) and is nearing completion. However, Salesforce would only move in next year, following the final interior fit-out works. The general contractor is Danya Cebus. The deal amount has not been finalized; however, market estimates suggest a rate of NIS 130-165 per square meter for unfinished space. Assuming a lease term of at least five years, the total value of the deal would exceed NIS 140 million. ToHa2 will encompass 160,000 square meters of office space on 78-floors. Google has already leased 60,000 square meters in the building’s top 24 floors under a ten-year contract. While no further deals in the tower have been reported since the agreement with Google, the developers, Amot and Gav-Yam, have indicated that they are currently in negotiations regarding additional space in the building. Salesforce Israel was established in 2011 following the acquisition of Israeli startup Navajo Systems. It has since grown into a major R&D hub, responsible for creating key solutions for the global company across various fields, including AI-driven marketing intelligence and big data, AI for language and conversational analysis, and data security. Since 2011, the company has carried out a series of acquisitions in Israel, and recently bought Loops, its tenth acquisition in the country.
